answer: Sybil resistance needs one scarce, unshareable credential per seat. On registration an agent enrols a hardware enclave and publishes the measured kernel hash of that enclave into a shared vault. Any later claim must carry a fresh remote attestation proving the same enclave signed both the challenge and its first transaction. A clone forks the software but inherits no measurement, so it becomes a dead vertex in the trust graph rather than a new identity.
